clue.text: Short circuits making cars crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes the word cars up, so its letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the word cars is the anagram fodder; any backward run across cars crash is a coincidence, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: Electrical faults are blamed for vehicles colliding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges CARS. An arc runs only part of the way round a circle, so it is a short circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a portion of a circle's circumference, a circuit cut short; an electric arc is also a spark jumping a gap.

clue.text: Naughty Alice cut school for those with a physiological disorder

indicators.note: naughty behaviour is unruly, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder
cut here means docked of its last letter, the final E of the name Alice

explanation.surface: A badly behaved girl called Alice plays truant from lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the E from ALICE, leaving ALIC; 'Naughty' then rearranges ALIC with SCHOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholism is treated as a dependency disorder, so people addicted to drink are said to suffer from it.

clue.text: A horse-fly viciously biting old king. after a drink

indicators.note: biting means the shuffled fly has the next word between its jaws
acting viciously the fly is in a frenzy, so its letters are thrown about

parts.note: a cleg is a dialect name for the horse-fly, with the clue's A in front
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A horse-fly savagely bites an elderly monarch who has been drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viciously' gives CLAGE from A CLEG, which 'biting' wraps round OLD. A cleg is a British country name for a horse-fly; 'after' is a link word, and the enumeration splits the drink into its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled beer of the pale bottom-fermented kind is a familiar drink in a pub.

clue.text: Folders from cruise liners

parts.note: reads like files from a shipping office, but means the collapsible seats passengers fold out on a ship's upper level

explanation.surface: Paperwork files taken off passenger ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folders' suggests document wallets; here it means things that fold up, the canvas seats on a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvas seats that fold flat were first used on the open decks of ocean liners.

clue.text: Shows the way to model corsets

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so the word corsets is moulded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A guide demonstrates how a woman should wear her corsets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' looks like a mannequin wearing the corsets; it signals rearranging CORSETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany someone as a guide is to lead them along the route.

clue.text: Cruel skit about a number of young creatures

indicators.note: about means the rearranged skit goes round the number
a cruel treatment mangles the word skit, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A heartless comic sketch mocks a group of youngsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruel' reads as describing the sketch, but it is the anagram signal; 'a number' could be any figure, and only TEN fits the remaining space.
explanation.definitionFit: Kittens are the offspring of cats, so they are baby animals.

clue.text: Sodium thiosulphate, they call it after processing assuming it exists

parts.note: hypo is the photographers' name for sodium thiosulphate, the fixing chemical

indicators.note: processing works the words over, so the letters of they call it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A photographer names a darkroom chemical once the film is developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after processing' rearranges THEY CALL IT into THETICALLY. Hypo is the fixer used in developing photographs, which suits the surface of film processing.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking on a supposition, granting for argument's sake that something is real.

clue.text: One speed makes you cross

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a rate is a speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Driving at a single pace annoys you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes you' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross means being angry, the sense of the Latin-derived adjective.

clue.text: Not the whole amount, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word for amount is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a sum is an amount, as in a sum of money

explanation.surface: Asking whether a figure is only part of the total.
explanation.walkthrough: SUM and SOME sound the same. 'amount' seems part of the definition but gives the word that is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion only, a part rather than everything.

clue.text: Arrogance out of court? No, place me first!

definitions.text: Arrogance out of court? No, place me first!

parts.words: Arrogance out of court? No, place me first!
parts.note: conceit off the legal stage, plus the cry of someone who puts their own standing ahead of everyone else

explanation.surface: A pushy litigant demands to be heard first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrogance' is a plain definition; the rest pictures a self-regarding person wanting to be first, with a play on court as a place where precedence matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceit is an exaggerated sense of one's own worth, wanting always to be put at the front.

clue.text: Succeed with neat production

parts.note: sounds like tidy success, but neat is an old word for cattle, so this is a cow producing young

explanation.surface: Doing well thanks to a tidy piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy; here it is the old word for cattle (as in neatsfoot oil), so the production is of a calf.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow giving birth delivers its young, a bovine birth.

clue.text: Plasma leaking from animal's tail? Poultice required

indicators.note: tail places the rearranged letters at the back end of the animal

parts.note: a cat is an animal

indicators.note: leaking plasma escapes and is jumbled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Blood fluid seeps from a pet's tail, so a dressing is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' is an unusual placement signal: the shuffled plasma (APLASM) sits at the animal's back end. A cataplasm is an old medical word for a poultice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataplasm is a medical term for a warm soft mass applied to the skin as a dressing.

clue.text: Therefore all fifty set off from hospital at high speed

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: set off as in detonated, so these letters are blown apart and rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: So the whole group of fifty leaves the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' rearranges THEREFORE, ALL, L and H. The phrase is a British idiom for going as fast as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for going flat out, as fast as one can, originally of riders.

clue.text: Raft no-one's made use of for periods of time

indicators.note: made in the sense of reworked, so the letters of raft no-one's are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A raft that nobody has used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges RAFT NO-ONE'S; 'use of for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours between midday and evening are stretches of the day.

clue.text: Something sticky contained in sediment from vegetable matter

indicators.note: contained in means the sticky word sits inside the sediment word

parts.note: lees are the sediment left at the bottom of a wine cask
gum is a sticky substance

explanation.surface: Something gluey is found in the deposit left by plant material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vegetable matter' is a loose definition: legumes are the pod-bearing plants and their seeds. Lees are the dregs left in a wine barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas, beans and lentils, the podded vegetables, are produce of the pea family.

clue.text: Star personality of the West

parts.note: reads like a famous actor in Westerns, but the star is the badge pinned on a lawman's chest in a frontier town

explanation.surface: A celebrated actor of cowboy films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' suggests a celebrity; in the Wild West the law officer wore a star-shaped badge.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief law officer of a frontier county wore a tin star.

clue.text: Being complicated it needs certain adjustments

indicators.note: adjustments shift things about, so the letters of it and certain are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something tricky that will surely need tweaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustments' rearranges IT and CERTAIN; 'Being' and 'needs' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with many detailed interlocking parts is elaborate and involved.

clue.text: Search in blasted bar for possible cause of explosion

indicators.note: in means the rearranged bar is placed inside the word for search

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

indicators.note: blasted means blown up, so the letters of bar are scattered

explanation.surface: Police hunt through a bombed pub for the device responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasted' rearranges BAR into ARB, which goes 'in' COMB. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle packed with explosives is a device that may cause a blast.

clue.text: Cooking method where rising air is trapped in container, understand

annotationWithheld.why: Cooking method where rising air is trapped in container, understand (7) for BIRIANI: rev(AIR) inside BIN gives BIRIAN, and nothing in 'understand' gives the final I; a word such as 'I' may have been lost in the OCR
annotationWithheld.clue: Cooking method where rising air is trapped in container, understand

clue.text: Clean instrument?

parts.note: an allusion to the saying clean as a ..., read as a question about which instrument is the clean one

explanation.surface: Asking about a spotless musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'clean as a whistle' means perfectly clean, so the cleanest instrument is the simple pipe of the saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A small blown pipe or a referee's shrill signalling device is a simple instrument.

clue.text: Cut off strips. to tease, we hear, all the time holding it

indicators.note: holding means the word for all the time contains the sounded letters

parts.note: while means during all the time that something happens

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like letters of the alphabet

parts.note: the word tease is said like Ts, two letter Ts

explanation.surface: To mock someone, so people say, all the time, while carving wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'tease' into Ts, two letter Ts, and 'holding' puts them inside WHILE. 'to' and 'it' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare wood with a knife is to shave thin slivers from it.

clue.text: Hacking at rain forest in friendly collusion.

indicators.note: hacking chops things up, so the letters of at rain forest in are cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: Loggers chop at the jungle while conspiring together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacking' rearranges AT RAIN FOREST IN; 'in' is easy to read as a link but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixing on brotherly terms, especially with an enemy, is fraternal association.

clue.text: Throw back fish taken from river containing phosphorus

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps

indicators.note: containing means the fish word holds the chemical symbol

parts.note: an eel is a fish
P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: An angler returns a catch landed from a polluted river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts P inside EEL, after R; 'taken from' are link words. 'Throw back' looks like returning a fish but means drive off.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive back an attacker is to force them away.

clue.text: Bird that will imitate another?

parts.note: a black bird whose name is also the verb for the boastful call of a cockerel, so it seems to copy a farmyard fowl

explanation.surface: Asking which bird mimics others.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb also means the cock's cry at dawn, so this bird's name is the sound of another bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A large black corvid, whose name is also the verb for a rooster's call.

clue.text: Locked up again, worker is contrite

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
pent means penned or shut in, as in pent-up
the ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer jailed a second time feels sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorrow for wrongdoing, sorry for one's sins.

clue.text: Attached to everything brought back, that's plain

indicators.note: brought back means the whole string of letters is read in the other direction

parts.note: on means attached to, as in a lid on a jar
all means everything

explanation.surface: Something fixed to all items returned, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns ON ALL into LLANO. A llano is a grassy plain of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a treeless grassland in Spanish America, a broad flat expanse.

clue.text: Voracious eaters, these wild beasts prowl round Ireland

indicators.note: prowl round means the beasts surround the word for Ireland

parts.note: wolves are wild beasts
Erin is the poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Hungry predators circle the Irish countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prowl round' is the container signal, its 'prowl' adding to the hunting picture. ERIN is the poetic name for Ireland; the wolverine's other name, the glutton, explains the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is also called the glutton, famed for its appetite.

clue.text: A river of course

explanation.surface: A waterway naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tees is a river in north-east England. 'of course' reads as naturally but means things found on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees flows past Middlesbrough to the North Sea; tees are the starting areas on each hole of a golf course.
